 Order
The present Appeal seeks to challenge the Award dated 10.01.2022 passed by the learned Presiding Officer MACT (South-East), Saket Court, New Delhi [hereinafter referred to as "Impugned Order"].

By the Impugned Order, the Claim Petition filed by the Appellant/Claimant before the learned Tribunal was dismissed with a finding that the Claimant/Appellant could not prove that the accident happened due to rash and negligent driving.

2. Learned Counsel appearing on behalf of the Appellant has contended that:
(i) this is a case of an accident which caused death of an 18-year-old boy.
The boy was riding as a pillion rider on a scooty and met with an accident on 12.07.2015.
The deceased succumbed to injuries on 13.07.2015.
The Appellant filed a claim Petition before the Tribunal claiming compensation under the provisions of Section 166 of the MV Act against the insurer,

It is not disputed between the parties that the driver of the vehicle/Respondent No. 2 before the learned Tribunal was not traceable.
The only other eye witness of the accident was the Investigation Officer, who has also passed away during Covid.
He further submits that in view thereof, no witness could be produced before the learned Tribunal.

(ii) Relying on the provisions of Section 164 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 [hereinafter referred to as "MV Act"] the Counsel has stated that it is settled law that there is no bar in conversion of a Claim Petition filed under Section 166 of the MV Act to Petition under Section 163A of the MV Act.

2.1 It is stated by learned Counsel that the learned Tribunal had the liberty to convert the Petition filed Smt. Dasiya Devi vs M/S Icici Lombard Gic Ltd on 2 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/41222189/

2.2 Learned Counsel for the Appellant, in this behalf, seeks to rely upon the judgments United India Insurance Co. Ltd v. Rita Devi and Ors.; 2014 SCC OnLine Del 7523, New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
v. Shashi Negi & Ors.;2016 SCC OnLine Del 3044 and Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd v. Sh. Shiv Prasad Indramani @ Shiv Prasad Sharma @ Shiv Prasad Bhatt & Ors.; 2024 SCC OnLine Del 3960 passed by a Coordinate Bench of this Court to submit that Section 164 of the MV Act commences with a non obstante clause and thus has an overriding effect and since this is a beneficial legislation, the provisions of the MV Act should be interpreted liberally.
